analyst_view.overall: Leeds (12th, 11 points) are winless in five league games, have scored only two goals in that run and have drawn five of nine; Daniel Farke is under some scrutiny. Tottenham under Roberto De Zerbi have won three in a row (Coventry, Chelsea, Crystal Palace), scoring seven and conceding one. Leeds have injury doubts over Noah Okafor (groin, reported out), Anton Stach (foot), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (foot) and Joe Rodon, while Spurs are without Bergvall, Mudryk, Adarabioyo, Odobert and Xavi Simons, with James Maddison and Micky van de Ven reported as fitness concerns.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Leeds have scored just twice in their last five games and could be without Okafor, Stach and possibly Calvert-Lewin, which takes most of their threat away. Spurs have conceded once in three games and are short of attacking players with Simons, Odobert and Mudryk out and Maddison a doubt.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Spurs should have more of the ball, but the injuries on both sides do not clearly change how often each team gets into wide areas.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, already raised for John Brooks's record. Reports differ on whether Rodrigo Bentancur is still suspended or back on the bench, and nothing else in the news points the number either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. A Leeds attack missing Okafor and maybe Stach and Calvert-Lewin has been blunt for weeks, and Spurs are without several creative players, so the total looks a little high.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. With Leeds scoring twice in five games and Spurs short of Simons, Odobert and possibly Maddison, clean chances may be scarce.
